sanskrit: tasminn uparate śabde bhīmaseno 'bravīd idam pragṛhya vipulaṃ vṛttaṃ bhujaṃ candanarūṣitam
english: When that noise had subsided, Bhīmasena spoke thus, raising his great round arm smeared with sandalwood paste.

sanskrit: yady eṣa gurur asmākaṃ dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ na prabhuḥ syāt kulasyāsya na vayaṃ marṣayemahi
english: If this Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira, our elder, were not the master of this family, we would not endure this.

sanskrit: īśo naḥ puṇyatapasāṃ prāṇānām api ceśvaraḥ manyate jitam ātmānaṃ yady eṣa vijitā vayam
english: He is the lord of our virtuous austerities and even our very lives. If he considers himself conquered, then we are conquered.

sanskrit: na hi mucyeta jīvan me padā bhūmim upaspṛśan martyadharmā parāmṛśya pāñcālyā mūrdhajān imān
english: He who, being subject to the law of mortals, has touched these tresses of the Pāñcālī lady, could not escape alive if he merely touched the earth with my foot.

sanskrit: paśyadhvam āyatau vṛttau bhujau me parighāv iva naitayor antaraṃ prāpya mucyetāpi śatakratuḥ
english: Behold my two long, round arms like iron bars — even Indra of a hundred sacrifices, caught between them, could not escape.

sanskrit: dharmapāśasitas tv evaṃ nādhigacchāmi saṃkaṭam gauraveṇa niruddhaś ca nigrahād arjunasya ca
english: But bound as I am by the bonds of dharma, I cannot find my way through this crisis, restrained also by respect and by Arjuna's restraint.

sanskrit: dharmarājanisṛṣṭas tu siṃhaḥ kṣudramṛgān iva dhārtarāṣṭrān imān pāpān niṣpiṣeyaṃ talāsibhiḥ
english: Released by the king of dharma, I would crush these sinful sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra like a lion crushing small deer with the flat of my sword.

sanskrit: tam uvāca tadā bhīṣmo droṇo vidura eva ca kṣamyatām evam ity evaṃ sarvaṃ saṃbhavati tvayi
english: Then Bhīṣma, Droṇa, and Vidura all said to him: "Forgive — it is so — all this is possible in you."

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca trayaḥ kileme adhanā bhavanti; dāsaḥ śiṣyaś cāsvatantrā ca nārī dāsasya patnī tvaṃ dhanam asya bhadre; hīneśvarā dāsadhanaṃ ca dāsī
english: Karṇa said: There are indeed three who are propertyless — a slave, a student, and a woman without independence. You, dear lady, are the property of a slave, the wife of a slave; you are low, the wealth of a slave, yourself a slave-woman.

sanskrit: praviśya sā naḥ paricārair bhajasva; tat te kāryaṃ śiṣṭam āveśya veśma īśāḥ sma sarve tava rājaputri; bhavanti te dhārtarāṣṭrā na pārthāḥ
english: Enter and serve us with your attendance; that is the remaining duty for you — go into the household. We are all your masters now, princess; the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra are yours, not the Pārthas.

sanskrit: anyaṃ vṛṇīṣva patim āśu bhāmini; yasmād dāsyaṃ na labhase devanena anavadyā vai patiṣu kāmavṛttir; nityaṃ dāsye viditaṃ vai tavāstu
english: Choose another husband quickly, O beautiful one, from whom you will not obtain slavery through gambling. Indeed, a blameless woman's freedom among husbands is known in the Vedas — let that be always known to you as slavery now.

sanskrit: parājito nakulo bhīmaseno; yudhiṣṭhiraḥ sahadevo 'rjunaś ca dāsībhūtā praviśa yājñaseni; parājitās te patayo na santi
english: Nakula has been defeated, and Bhīmasena, Yudhiṣṭhira, Sahadeva, and Arjuna — enter as a slave-woman, Yājñasenī; your husbands are defeated, they are no more.

sanskrit: prayojanaṃ cātmani kiṃ nu manyate; parākramaṃ pauruṣaṃ ceha pārthaḥ pāñcālyasya drupadasyātmajām imāṃ; sabhāmadhye yo 'tidevīd glaheṣu
english: And what purpose does the Pārtha think he serves with his own valor and manhood here — he who staked this daughter of Drupada, the Pāñcālī princess, in the assembly's gambling?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tad vai śrutvā bhīmaseno 'tyamarṣī; bhṛśaṃ niśaśvāsa tadārtarūpaḥ rājānugo dharmapāśānubaddho; dahann ivainaṃ kopaviraktadṛṣṭiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing that, Bhīmasena, deeply wrathful, sighed heavily, showing a tormented form; following the king, bound by the cords of dharma, he seemed to burn Karṇa with his eyes reddened by anger.

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca nāhaṃ kupye sūtaputrasya rājann; eṣa satyaṃ dāsadharmaḥ praviṣṭaḥ kiṃ vidviṣo vādya māṃ dhārayeyur; nādevīs tvaṃ yady anayā narendra
english: Bhīma said: I do not grow angry at the son of a charioteer, O king — this truth of slave-law has entered. For what could those who hate me do to restrain me today — if only you had not gambled with her, O lord of men.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca rādheyasya vacaḥ śrutvā rājā duryodhanas tadā yudhiṣṭhiram uvācedaṃ tūṣṇīṃbhūtam acetasam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the words of Rādheya (Karṇa), King Duryodhana then said this to Yudhiṣṭhira, who had fallen silent and was senseless:

sanskrit: bhīmārjunau yamau caiva sthitau te nṛpa śāsane praśnaṃ prabrūhi kṛṣṇāṃ tvam ajitāṃ yadi manyase
english: "Bhīma, Arjuna, and the twin brothers are standing under your command, O king. Speak the answer to the question yourself — do you consider Kṛṣṇa (Draupadī) to be unconquered?"

sanskrit: evam uktvā sa kaunteyam apohya vasanaṃ svakam smayann ivaikṣat pāñcālīm aiśvaryamadamohitaḥ
english: Having said this, he cast aside his own garment and, as if smiling, looked at the Pāñcālī woman, deluded by the intoxication of lordship.

sanskrit: kadalīdaṇḍasadṛśaṃ sarvalakṣaṇapūjitam gajahastapratīkāśaṃ vajrapratimagauravam
english: His thigh, resembling the trunk of a banana tree, adorned with all auspicious marks, like the trunk of an elephant, with the weight and solidity of a thunderbolt —

sanskrit: abhyutsmayitvā rādheyaṃ bhīmam ādharṣayann iva draupadyāḥ prekṣamāṇāyāḥ savyam ūrum adarśayat
english: — smiling scornfully at Rādheya and as if challenging Bhīma, he displayed his left thigh to the watching Draupadī.

sanskrit: vṛkodaras tad ālokya netre utphālya lohite provāca rājamadhye taṃ sabhāṃ viśrāvayann iva
english: Vṛkodara (Bhīma), seeing that, widened his eyes until they were bloodshot, and spoke in the midst of the kings, as if making the assembly hear:

sanskrit: pitṛbhiḥ saha sālokyaṃ mā sma gacched vṛkodaraḥ yady etam ūruṃ gadayā na bhindyāṃ te mahāhave
english: "Let Vṛkodara not attain the same world as his fathers if I do not shatter this thigh of yours with my mace in the great battle!"

sanskrit: kruddhasya tasya srotobhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāvakārciṣaḥ vṛkṣasyeva viniśceruḥ koṭarebhyaḥ pradahyataḥ
english: From all the apertures of that enraged man, flames of fire poured forth, like from the hollows of a burning tree.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca paraṃ bhayaṃ paśyata bhīmasenād; budhyadhvaṃ rājño varuṇasyeva pāśāt daiverito nūnam ayaṃ purastāt; paro 'nayo bharateṣūdapādi
english: Vidura said: See the great fear from Bhīmasena! Understand — it is like the noose of King Varuṇa. Surely this great calamity has arisen before us among the Bhāratas, driven by fate.

sanskrit: atidyūtaṃ kṛtam idaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrā; ye 'syāṃ striyaṃ vivadadhvaṃ sabhāyām yogakṣemo dṛśyate vo mahābhayaḥ; pāpān mantrān kuravo mantrayanti
english: O sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, this gambling has gone too far. You who are quarreling over this woman in the assembly — great danger is seen for your welfare and security. The Kurus are taking evil counsel.

sanskrit: imaṃ dharmaṃ kuravo jānatāśu; durdṛṣṭe 'smin pariṣat saṃpraduṣyet imāṃ cet pūrvaṃ kitavo 'glahīṣyad; īśo 'bhaviṣyad aparājitātmā
english: Know this dharma quickly, O Kurus! In this evil sight, the assembly would become corrupted. If the gambler had staked her first (before himself), he would have been the lord with an unconquered self.

sanskrit: svapne yathaitad dhi dhanaṃ jitaṃ syāt; tad evaṃ manye yasya dīvyaty anīśaḥ gāndhāriputrasya vaco niśamya; dharmād asmāt kuravo māpayāta
english: Just as wealth won in a dream is unreal — I think the same of the winning of one who gambles without being his own master. Having heard the son of Gāndhārī's words, O Kurus, do not stray from this dharma.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca bhīmasya vākye tadvad evārjunasya; sthito 'haṃ vai yamayoś caivam eva yudhiṣṭhiraṃ cet pravadanty anīśam; atho dāsyān mokṣyase yājñaseni
english: Duryodhana said: I stand by Bhīma's words and likewise Arjuna's, and by those of the twins too. If they declare Yudhiṣṭhira to be his own master, then Yājñasenī, you shall be freed from slavery.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca īśo rājā pūrvam āsīd glahe naḥ; kuntīputro dharmarājo mahātmā īśas tv ayaṃ kasya parājitātmā; taj jānīdhvaṃ kuravaḥ sarva eva
english: Arjuna said: The king was the master in our gambling — the great-souled Dharmarāja, son of Kuntī. But now this master, whose self has been defeated — of whom is he master? Know this, all you Kurus.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato rājño dhṛtarāṣṭrasya gehe; gomāyur uccair vyāharad agnihotre taṃ rāsabhāḥ pratyabhāṣanta rājan; samantataḥ pakṣiṇaś caiva raudrāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, O king, in King Dhṛtarāṣṭra's house, a jackal cried out loudly at the sacred fire; donkeys brayed in response to it, and fierce birds cried out all around.

sanskrit: taṃ ca śabdaṃ viduras tattvavedī; śuśrāva ghoraṃ subalātmajā ca bhīṣmadroṇau gautamaś cāpi vidvān; svasti svastīty api caivāhur uccaiḥ
english: That terrible sound was heard by Vidura, the knower of truth, and by Subala's daughter (Gāndhārī), and by Bhīṣma, Droṇa, and the learned Gautama — and they all cried out "Svasti! Svasti!" (May there be peace!) loudly.

sanskrit: tato gāndhārī viduraś caiva vidvāṃs; tam utpātaṃ ghoram ālakṣya rājñe nivedayām āsatur ārtavat tadā; tato rājā vākyam idaṃ babhāṣe
english: Then Gāndhārī and the wise Vidura, observing that terrible omen, reported it to the king with distress; and then the king spoke these words:

sanskrit: hato 'si duryodhana mandabuddhe; yas tvaṃ sabhāyāṃ kurupuṃgavānām striyaṃ samābhāṣasi durvinīta; viśeṣato draupadīṃ dharmapatnīm
english: "You are destroyed, Duryodhana, dull-witted one! You who address a woman in the assembly of the Kuru chiefs, O ill-mannered one — and especially Draupadī, the dharma-devoted wife."

sanskrit: evam uktvā dhṛtarāṣṭro manīṣī; hitānveṣī bāndhavānām apāyāt kṛṣṇāṃ pāñcālīm abravīt sāntvapūrvaṃ; vimṛśyaitat prajñayā tattvabuddhiḥ
english: Having said this, the wise Dhṛtarāṣṭra, seeker of the welfare of his kinsmen, departed; then he spoke with conciliation to Kṛṣṇa the Pāñcālī woman, having considered the matter with his wisdom and true discernment.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca varaṃ vṛṇīṣva pāñcāli matto yad abhikāṅkṣasi vadhūnāṃ hi viśiṣṭā me tvaṃ dharmaparamā satī
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Choose a boon from me, Pāñcālī — whatever you desire; for among my daughters-in-law you are foremost, devoted to dharma, a good woman.

sanskrit: draupady uvāca dadāsi ced varaṃ mahyaṃ vṛṇomi bharatarṣabha sarvadharmānugaḥ śrīmān adāso 'stu yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Draupadī said: If you grant me a boon, O bull of the Bhāratas, I choose this: let the glorious Yudhiṣṭhira, follower of all dharma, be no slave.

sanskrit: manasvinam ajānanto mā vai brūyuḥ kumārakāḥ eṣa vai dāsaputreti prativindhyaṃ tam āgatam
english: So that children, not knowing him to be a noble soul, may not say of Prativindhya as he comes to them: 'This is the son of a slave.'

sanskrit: rājaputraḥ purā bhūtvā yathā nānyaḥ pumān kva cit lālito dāsaputratvaṃ paśyan naśyed dhi bhārata
english: Having been a prince before, pampered as no other man anywhere — seeing himself become the son of a slave, he would surely perish, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca dvitīyaṃ te varaṃ bhadre dadāmi varayasva mām mano hi me vitarati naikaṃ tvaṃ varam arhasi
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: A second boon I give you, dear lady — ask it of me; for my mind is pleased and you deserve more than one boon.

sanskrit: draupady uvāca sarathau sadhanuṣkau ca bhīmasenadhanaṃjayau nakulaṃ sahadevaṃ ca dvitīyaṃ varaye varam
english: Draupadī said: As a second boon I choose Bhīmasena and Dhanañjaya, both with their chariots and bows, and Nakula and Sahadeva.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tṛtīyaṃ varayāsmatto nāsi dvābhyāṃ susatkṛtā tvaṃ hi sarvasnuṣāṇāṃ me śreyasī dharmacāriṇī
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Choose a third boon from me — you are not honored by just two; for among all my daughters-in-law you are the best, a walker of the path of dharma.

sanskrit: draupady uvāca lobho dharmasya nāśāya bhagavan nāham utsahe anarhā varam ādātuṃ tṛtīyaṃ rājasattama
english: Draupadī said: Greed destroys dharma, my lord; I do not venture to accept an undeserved boon — I am unworthy to take a third boon, O best of kings.

sanskrit: ekam āhur vaiśyavaraṃ dvau tu kṣatrastriyā varau trayas tu rājño rājendra brāhmaṇasya śataṃ varāḥ
english: They say a Vaiśya woman merits one boon, a Kṣatriya woman two boons, a king three boons, O king of kings, and for a Brahmin, a hundred boons.

sanskrit: pāpīyāṃsa ime bhūtvā saṃtīrṇāḥ patayo mama vetsyanti caiva bhadrāṇi rājan puṇyena karmaṇā
english: My husbands, having been made sinful, are now rescued; they will know all good things through meritorious deeds, O king.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca yā naḥ śrutā manuṣyeṣu striyo rūpeṇa saṃmatāḥ tāsām etādṛśaṃ karma na kasyāṃ cana śuśrumaḥ
english: Karṇa said: Among women honored for their beauty among men — we have never heard of such a deed as this by any of them.

sanskrit: krodhāviṣṭeṣu pārtheṣu dhārtarāṣṭreṣu cāpy ati draupadī pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ kṛṣṇā śāntir ihābhavat
english: While the Pārthas were seized by anger, and the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra were too, Draupadī — Kṛṣṇa — became the peace of the sons of Pāṇḍu here.

sanskrit: aplave 'mbhasi magnānām apratiṣṭhe nimajjatām pāñcālī pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ naur eṣā pāragābhavat
english: For the sons of Pāṇḍu sinking in waters without a raft, drowning in the fathomless deep, this Pāñcālī woman became the boat that took them to the other shore.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tad vai śrutvā bhīmasenaḥ kurumadhye 'tyamarṣaṇaḥ strī gatiḥ pāṇḍuputrāṇām ity uvāca sudurmanāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing that, Bhīmasena, deeply wrathful in the midst of the Kurus, said with great anguish: "A woman is the resort of the sons of Pāṇḍu!"

sanskrit: trīṇi jyotīṃṣi puruṣa iti vai devalo 'bravīt apatyaṃ karma vidyā ca yataḥ sṛṣṭāḥ prajās tataḥ
english: "Three lights of a man," Devala indeed said: "offspring, deeds, and learning — from these the people are created."

sanskrit: amedhye vai gataprāṇe śūnye jñātibhir ujjhite dehe tritayam evaitat puruṣasyopajāyate
english: "These three of a man are reborn from a body that has become impure, that has lost life, that is empty, abandoned by kinsmen."

sanskrit: tan no jyotir abhihataṃ dārāṇām abhimarśanāt dhanaṃjaya kathaṃ svit syād apatyam abhimṛṣṭajam
english: "That light of ours has been struck down by the touching of our wives, Dhanañjaya — how indeed could there be offspring born of the defiled?"

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca na caivoktā na cānuktā hīnataḥ paruṣā giraḥ bhāratāḥ pratijalpanti sadā tūttamapūruṣāḥ
english: Arjuna said: Whether addressed or unaddressed, cruel and base words — the highest men among the Bhāratas never babble such things back; the truly excellent men do so always.

sanskrit: smaranti sukṛtāny eva na vairāṇi kṛtāni ca santaḥ prativijānanto labdhvā pratyayam ātmanaḥ
english: The good, responding rightly and having gained certainty within themselves, remember only the good deeds done to them, never the enmities.

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca ihaivaitāṃs turā sarvān hanmi śatrūn samāgatān atha niṣkramya rājendra samūlān kṛndhi bhārata
english: Bhīma said: Right here I will swiftly slay all these enemies gathered together — or, having gone out, cut them down root and all, O king of kings, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kiṃ no vivaditeneha kiṃ naḥ kleśena bhārata adyaivaitān nihanmīha praśādhi vasudhām imām
english: What is the use of arguing here? What is the use of suffering, O Bhārata? This very day I will slay them here — command us over this earth.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity uktvā bhīmasenas tu kaniṣṭhair bhrātṛbhir vṛtaḥ mṛgamadhye yathā siṃho muhuḥ parigham aikṣata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having said this, Bhīmasena, surrounded by his younger brothers, looked repeatedly at his iron bar as a lion among deer.

sanskrit: sāntvyamāno vījyamānaḥ pārthenākliṣṭakarmaṇā svidyate ca mahābāhur antardāhena vīryavān
english: Being soothed and fanned by Arjuna of untiring action, the mighty-armed hero, powerful in valor, sweated with the inner burning of his rage.

sanskrit: kruddhasya tasya srotobhyaḥ karṇādibhyo narādhipa sadhūmaḥ sasphuliṅgārciḥ pāvakaḥ samajāyata
english: From all the apertures of that enraged man — from his ears and the rest, O lord of men — fire arose with smoke and sparks and flames.

sanskrit: bhrukuṭīpuṭaduṣprekṣyam abhavat tasya tan mukham yugāntakāle saṃprāpte kṛtāntasyeva rūpiṇaḥ
english: His face, terrible to behold with its knitted brows, became like that of Death personified when the end of a cosmic age has arrived.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tam āvārya bāhunā bāhuśālinam maivam ity abravīc cainaṃ joṣam āssveti bhārata
english: Yudhiṣṭhira, restraining that mighty-armed one with his own arm, said to him: "Do not do so" — and "Be still," O Bhārata.

sanskrit: nivārya taṃ mahābāhuṃ kopasaṃraktalocanam pitaraṃ samupātiṣṭhad dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: Having restrained that mighty-armed one whose eyes were reddened with anger, he approached his elder Dhṛtarāṣṭra with folded hands.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca rājan kiṃ karavāmas te praśādhy asmāṃs tvam īśvaraḥ nityaṃ hi sthātum icchāmas tava bhārata śāsane
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: O king, what shall we do for you? Command us — you are the lord. We always wish to remain under your command, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ajātaśatro bhadraṃ te ariṣṭaṃ svasti gacchata anujñātāḥ sahadhanāḥ svarājyam anuśāsata
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: May good fortune be yours, Ajātaśatru — go unharmed, in peace. You are hereby dismissed with your wealth; rule your own kingdom.

sanskrit: idaṃ tv evāvaboddhavyaṃ vṛddhasya mama śāsanam dhiyā nigaditaṃ kṛtsnaṃ pathyaṃ niḥśreyasaṃ param
english: But this teaching of mine, an old man, is to be understood: it is spoken with wisdom in full, beneficial, and supremely for your wellbeing.

sanskrit: vettha tvaṃ tāta dharmāṇāṃ gatiṃ sūkṣmāṃ yudhiṣṭhira vinīto 'si mahāprājña vṛddhānāṃ paryupāsitā
english: You know the subtle course of dharmas, dear Yudhiṣṭhira; you are well-bred, greatly wise, an attendant of the elders.

sanskrit: yato buddhis tataḥ śāntiḥ praśamaṃ gaccha bhārata nādārau kramate śastraṃ dārau śastraṃ nipātyate
english: Where there is wisdom, there is peace — seek calm, O Bhārata. A weapon does not move against what is not split; a weapon is brought down only against what is split (divided).

sanskrit: na vairāṇy abhijānanti guṇān paśyanti nāguṇān virodhaṃ nādhigacchanti ye ta uttamapūruṣāḥ
english: Those highest of men do not know enmities, do not see faults but only virtues, and do not arrive at opposition.

sanskrit: saṃvāde paruṣāṇy āhur yudhiṣṭhira narādhamāḥ pratyāhur madhyamās tv etān uktāḥ paruṣam uttaram
english: In a dispute, the basest of men speak harsh words, O Yudhiṣṭhira; the middling, when spoken to harshly, speak harsh words in return.

sanskrit: naivoktā naiva cānuktā ahitāḥ paruṣā giraḥ pratijalpanti vai dhīrāḥ sadā uttamapūruṣāḥ
english: Whether addressed or not addressed, the wise — the highest of men — never babble back hostile, harsh words; this is always so.

sanskrit: smaranti sukṛtāny eva na vairāṇi kṛtāny api santaḥ prativijānanto labdhvā pratyayam ātmanaḥ
english: The good, responding rightly and having gained certainty within themselves, remember only the kind deeds done to them, never the enmities inflicted.

sanskrit: tathācaritam āryeṇa tvayāsmin satsamāgame duryodhanasya pāruṣyaṃ tat tāta hṛdi mā kṛthāḥ
english: Such is the noble conduct you have shown in this assembly of the good — do not take Duryodhana's harshness to heart, dear son.

sanskrit: mātaraṃ caiva gāndhārīṃ māṃ ca tvadguṇakāṅkṣiṇam upasthitaṃ vṛddham andhaṃ pitaraṃ paśya bhārata
english: Regard also your mother Gāndhārī and me, longing for your virtues — your old, blind father who stands before you, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: prekṣāpūrvaṃ mayā dyūtam idam āsīd upekṣitam mitrāṇi draṣṭukāmena putrāṇāṃ ca balābalam
english: This gambling was overlooked by me after observation, desiring to see the strength and weakness of friends and of my sons.

sanskrit: aśocyāḥ kuravo rājan yeṣāṃ tvam anuśāsitā mantrī ca viduro dhīmān sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ
english: The Kurus need not be grieved over, O king, when you are their guide and Vidura, the wise counselor versed in all the shastras, is their minister.

sanskrit: tvayi dharmo 'rjune vīryaṃ bhīmasene parākramaḥ śraddhā ca guruśuśrūṣā yamayoḥ puruṣāgryayoḥ
english: In you resides dharma, in Arjuna valor, in Bhīmasena prowess; and faith and service to elders belong to the twin brothers, those foremost of men.

sanskrit: ajātaśatro bhadraṃ te khāṇḍavaprastham āviśa bhrātṛbhis te 'stu saubhrātraṃ dharme te dhīyatāṃ manaḥ
english: May good fortune be yours, Ajātaśatru — enter Khāṇḍavaprastha; let there be brotherhood among your brothers; let your mind be fixed on dharma.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity ukto bharataśreṣṭho dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ kṛtvāryasamayaṃ sarvaṃ pratasthe bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, the best of the Bhāratas, Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira, having made noble farewells to all, departed together with his brothers.

sanskrit: te rathān meghasaṃkāśān āsthāya saha kṛṣṇayā prayayur hṛṣṭamanasa indraprasthaṃ purottamam
english: Mounting their cloud-like chariots together with Kṛṣṇa (Draupadī), they set out with joyful minds toward Indraprastha, the foremost of cities.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca anujñātāṃs tān viditvā saratnadhanasaṃcayān pāṇḍavān dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ katham āsīn manas tadā
english: Janamejaya said: Knowing those Pāṇḍavas to have been dismissed along with their accumulated jewels and wealth, what was then the mind of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca anujñātāṃs tān viditvā dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa dhīmatā rājan duḥśāsanaḥ kṣipraṃ jagāma bhrātaraṃ prati
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Knowing those Pāṇḍavas to have been dismissed by the wise Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O king, Duḥśāsana quickly went to his brother.
